A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BG-HGNN and contain readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained methods, datasets, and analyses can be matched despite extensive rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification and link-prediction results in Tables 1–2, ablations, a meta-path case study, and appendix preprocessing measurements.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results in Tables 1 and 4, including additional baseline evaluations, and retains the ablations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The overall pipeline and Algorithms 1–3 persist. However, v1 Equation (3.9) combines projected factors using Kronecker products, whereas v2 Equation (3.1) specifies element-wise multiplication; v2 Algorithm 3 still uses Kronecker products. The PDFs do not resolve whether this corrects the description or changes the fusion procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight node-classification datasets and three link-prediction datasets, including the same 2-hop and random-hop tests. Freebase was already evaluated in v1 despite its omission from the main-text dataset list. Dynamic graphs remain future work.

E2.justification: v2 adds NARS and SlotGAT to the retained HGT, RGCN, and simple-HGN comparisons. Both added methods have reported node-classification results in Table 1 and link-prediction results under both testing scenarios in Table 4, substantially broadening the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Node-classification evaluation changes from micro-F1/macro-F1 to accuracy/precision throughout Table 1 and the experimental description. v2 also specifies node-type encoding dimension 10 times the number of node types, whereas v1 describes m-dimensional encodings with m node types. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun. Three-layer models and link-prediction metrics remain.

E4.justification: The encoding/fusion ablation has slightly revised plotted outcomes: for example, Concat + Random accuracy changes from approximately 86.6% to 87.2% in Figure 4(a). The tested variants and principal conclusions remain. Rank sensitivity, feature-combination ablations, preprocessing analysis, and the meta-path study are retained; v2 Figure 4(d) redisplays the existing appendix feature ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five independent trials. v2 Table 1 newly states that variances are small and similar across methods and therefore omitted. This adds qualitative uncertainty reporting, without numerical variances, confidence intervals, significance tests, or evidence of additional runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces classification scores under different metrics and revises parameter counts substantially: ACM HGT changes from 0.59 to 5.92 million parameters. BG-HGNN's listed IMDB throughput changes from 3.07x to 3.82x. NARS and SlotGAT results are added, alongside smaller changes in plotted analyses. Existing link-prediction scores are retained. The classification score replacements do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v1's O(|R|^L) HGNN scaling and O(rL) BG-HGNN scaling are replaced by Theta(|R| L D^2) and Theta((r+L) D^2), with explicit assumptions and a new proof. v2 corrects the reversed implication in Definition 1, introduces model-class and random-encoding assumptions, and replaces the brief expressiveness argument with Lemma A.1 and extensive proofs in Appendix A.

C1.justification: The central efficiency and expressiveness contribution remains. The headline throughput claim changes from 8.12x to 110.30x, although 110.30x already appeared in v1 Table 1. The quantified 1.07x accuracy claim becomes matching or surpassing baseline accuracy, and the introduction drops the explicit claim of being first to identify the two limitations.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the concluding discussion of projection-distribution choices and prospective graph foundation models with a specific limitation to static graphs and proposed dynamic, streaming, and continual-learning extensions. It also adds a distance-preservation and approximate-orthogonality rationale for random encodings. The meta-path interpretation remains in Appendix B.

D1.justification: v2 provides more explicit encoding and projection dimensions but removes v1's statement that featureless nodes receive random 256-dimensional features. Hardware specifications and the three implementation algorithms are retained. Zero padding in v2's main text matches the implementation already documented in v1's appendix, rather than establishing a new preprocessing procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for NARS, SlotGAT, other heterogeneous-graph methods, random-encoding motivation, GCN, and Freebase, while removing several multimodal-fusion references. The basic positioning relative to meta-path and message-passing approaches remains, with the explicit first-to-identify novelty claim removed.

P1.justification: The introduction, preliminaries, methodology, theory, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The method becomes four named components, experiments receive separate setup/results/ablation subsections, and the meta-path discussion moves to an appendix. The title, author list, terminology, and appendix organization also change.

P2.justification: v2 changes the page template, redraws Figures 1–2 and several plots, converts rank sensitivity from bars to a line, assembles a four-panel ablation figure, and expands tables with colored rankings. Link-prediction results move to the appendix. Some captions deteriorate: Figure 3 receives unrelated subcaptions, and the unchanged 4-by-4 meta-path heatmaps are described as 50-by-50 in Figure 5.

improvement.justification: Corrected parameter scaling, a corrected expressiveness definition, and additional baselines provide real benefits. However, the expanded expressiveness proof improperly infers equal expected nonlinear outputs from equal input means in Lemma A.1, and the revised fusion formula conflicts with retained pseudocode. Approximately tenfold parameter-count revisions are unexplained, while feature-initialization information is lost. These competing gains and unresolved soundness and reproducibility problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
